advisory.note: theological concerns for the owner: ¶12 (English source): "the Vedas, which He Himself created" (translated faithfully as தாமே படைத்த வேதங்கள்). In Sri Vaishnava doctrine the Vedas are apauruṣeya and eternal; the Lord reveals or brings them forth (as ¶4 itself says, 'came forth from His breath') rather than creating them. The owner may wish to revise the English (e.g. 'which came forth from Him'), after which the Tamil should follow.

advisory.note: theological concerns for the owner: ¶5 (English source): "must rely on bhakti yogam to reach the Lord" names bhakti yoga as the means for baddha souls without mentioning prapatti (śaraṇāgati), which Sri Vaishnava doctrine holds to be an independent and sufficient means. The Tamil now translates the English exactly (no added exclusivity); the owner may wish to qualify the English. | ¶7 (English source): "have earned a permanent place within the realm of Sri Vaikuntham" (Tamil: பெற்ற, neutral). 'Earned' suggests moksham is merited by the soul's effort rather than granted by the Lord's grace; the owner may prefer 'attained' or 'been granted' in the English.

advisory.note: theological concerns for the owner: Glossary warnings for 'released souls' in ¶2, ¶17, ¶21 and ¶25 are false positives. The text uses "मुक्त आत्माओं", the oblique plural of the glossary form मुक्त आत्माएँ, which Hindi grammar requires before को/की/द्वारा. The form is correct and should not change. | ¶5 (English): "must rely on bhakti yogam to reach the Lord" gives bhakti yoga as the only means for the bound souls and leaves out prapatti (śaraṇāgati). The Hindi renders it faithfully; the owner may wish to qualify the English. | ¶7 (English): "have earned a permanent place" in Sri Vaikuntham suggests that moksham is earned rather than granted by the Lord's grace. The Hindi "स्थायी स्थान पा लिया है" ('have obtained') already softens this; the owner may want to change the English to match.

advisory.note: theological concerns for the owner: ¶4 (English): "adorning the holy garland, Mukunda" makes Mukunda sound like the name of the garland, but in the verse (¶2) मुकुन्दः is the Lord. Following the convention, the Hindi "मुकुन्द नामक पावन माला" translates the English as written. The English should be corrected (for example 'the Lord, Mukunda, adorned with the holy garland'), and the Hindi should then be updated to match. | ¶4 (English): "Sri Vaikuntham, situated in the centre of the milky ocean" runs together Sri Vaikuntham and the Ksheerabdhi (vyūha) abode. The Hindi translates it faithfully; the owner should decide whether to change the English. | ¶8: For the English "creates such a beautiful vision of Himself", the Hindi now reads "अपना ऐसा सुन्दर दर्शन मुझे प्रदान करते हैं" ('grants me such a beautiful vision of Himself'). This avoids saying that His divine form is created, which round 1 had flagged, and I accept it. The owner should confirm that 'creates' may be softened to 'grants', or change the English the same way.
